analysis.brief_en: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) published a clinical overview of the monkeypox virus (MPXV) on August 19, 2026. The document highlights the two main clades of MPXV, clade I and clade II, which have different geographic distributions and transmission patterns. Clade I outbreaks began in Central Africa in 2024 and have spread globally through travel, while clade II outbreaks started in 2022 and are now endemic in over 100 countries. Both clades can be transmitted through close physical contact, including sexual contact, and can be treated and prevented similarly. However, clade I historically had a higher case-fatality rate, though recent data show it to be low with optimal care. Clade II has a lower fatality rate, with less than 0.1% mortality. The CDC recommends vaccines for prevention and post-exposure prophylaxis, along with thorough patient history and supportive care. Immunocompromised individuals, including children with malnutrition, are at higher risk of severe disease. The CDC also emphasizes the importance of testing for HIV in individuals suspected of having monkeypox.

title: Mpox outbreak in Guinea-Bissau sparks alarm: Children account for half of suspected cases, says UNICEF - Indiablooms

analysis.time: The outbreak was declared on 4 July (N5), and the news report was published on 2026-08-21 (N1). The suspected cases were identified as of August 21, 2026 (N1).
analysis.location_and_population: Guinea-Bissau, with a focus on children, particularly those under the age of four, who account for 16 out of the 46 suspected cases (N1).
analysis.event: A mpox outbreak in Guinea-Bissau has been reported, with children making up half of the suspected cases (N1). UNICEF has identified this as a major public health event (N2).

UNICEF urges families to seek immediate care if symptoms like rash, fever, or swollen lymph nodes appear and to follow preventive measures such as handwashing and avoiding close contact with suspected cases.

analysis.time: The outbreak was declared on 4 July 2026, and as of 17 August 2026, seven confirmed mpox cases have been reported. The publication date is 20 August 2026.
